title: Curves in Space and Their Tangents
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: Vector-Valued Function and Space Curve
definitions.latex: \mathbf{r}(t) = f(t)\mathbf{i} + g(t)\mathbf{j} + h(t)\mathbf{k} = \langle f(t), g(t), h(t) \rangle
definitions.statement: A vector-valued function r maps a real parameter t from an interval I into Euclidean space R^3. The set of terminal points of r(t) for t in I traces out a space curve C.
conditions: f, g, h are real functions defined on common interval I
definitions.explanation: Limits and continuity of r(t) are defined component-wise: lim r(t) = <lim f, lim g, lim h>.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Unifies particle trajectory kinematics and spatial curve geometry.

definitions.title: Derivative Vector and Unit Tangent Vector
definitions.latex: \mathbf{r}'(t) = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\mathbf{r}(t+\Delta t) - \mathbf{r}(t)}{\Delta t} = \langle f'(t), g'(t), h'(t) \rangle, \quad \mathbf{T}(t) = \frac{\mathbf{r}'(t)}{|\mathbf{r}'(t)|}
definitions.statement: The derivative vector r'(t) represents the instantaneous velocity vector v(t) tangent to the space curve pointing in the direction of increasing t. The unit tangent vector T(t) normalizes the velocity.
conditions: Curve is smooth: r'(t) is continuous and r'(t) != 0
definitions.explanation: The tangent line to the curve at t_0 has vector equation L(t) = r(t_0) + (t - t_0) r'(t_0).
definitions.keyTakeaway: T(t) captures the pure direction of motion independent of particle speed.
